On Sun, May 2, 2027 at 11:04 AM sergio_alvarez@redwood.com wrote:
> Proposed immediate next steps (please respond with availability):

> 2) Backfill strategy — parallel backfill with prefix/KV cache warmup...
> 3) Rerank evaluation plan — seed set, metrics...

Agree to the plan. I can own backfill design and execution. Initial notes below:

Backfill approach (draft):
- Stage 0: Snapshot current index (ids + payloads) and verify parity in staging.
- Stage 1: Incremental backfill into chosen vector DB written as immutable batches (to allow transactional rollback).
- Stage 2: Warm KV/prefix cache using synthetic traffic that mirrors peak token lengths.
- Stage 3: Canary cutover (1% traffic) with automatic fallback to legacy index for the first 48 hours.

Operational constraints to confirm with Acme SRE:
- Allowed RPS for backfill jobs over private link (we should throttle to avoid network saturation).
- Retention/Snapshot cadence for the old index.

I'll draft a runbook and a cron-based backfill orchestrator (Airflow job) with per-batch checksums and progress metrics. Attaching a starter spreadsheet with estimated durations per 100k records.

Monica
Senior Customer Success Engineer | Redwood Inference

[Attachment: acme_backfill_strategy_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

Thanks team — I'll lead the rerank evaluation. Initial plan:

Rerank eval (outline):
- Seedset: 2k real queries + 1k adversarial queries (typos, synonyms, cold-start items). Attached seedset CSV.
- Metrics: MAP@5, MRR, P@1, latency percentiles (p50/p95).
- Baselines: 1) Current lexical-only search, 2) Embeddings-only (dotprod) + current ranker, 3) Embeddings + light neural reranker (BERT-tiny).
- Acceptance criteria: MAP@5 improvement >= 8% and p95 latency increase <= 20ms vs embeddings-only baseline.

Rollout strategy:
- Phase A (staging eval): offline eval on seedset + QA user acceptance.
- Phase B (canary): 1% traffic with explicit telemetry (impressions -> click rates). 48 hour observation.
- Phase C: 10% -> 50% -> 100% based on telemetry windows and rollback health checks.

I'll instrument the eval harness and produce a one-pager with expected compute costs.

Marissa
Product Success Manager | Redwood Inference

[Attachment: rerank_eval_seedset.csv (CSV, 3.1MB)]

From: naomi_feldman@redwood.com
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-03T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Next steps for embeddings and rerank migration — cost + vector DB notes

Team — quick cost and vector-store recommendation notes for the kick-off meeting with Acme on Monday.

Vector DB considerations:
- Pinecone (managed): fastest path, predictable latency, but higher per-GB costs. Good if Acme wants minimal ops.
- Milvus (self-managed / k8s): lower unit-storage costs at scale, supports partitioning for TTL, but needs runbook for scaling and checkpointing.
- Faiss (self-hosted on VMs): best cost at scale for read-heavy workloads but requires custom sharding and recovery work.

Cost delta (very rough):
- Managed vector store + dedicated GPU capacity for rerank: +$12k–18k/month on top of current.
- Self-hosted Milvus + reserved infra: +$6k–9k/month but add 1 FTE for ops or dedicated SRE time.

Suggested default for Acme: start with Pinecone-managed for M0 canary (reduces risk), then migrate to Milvus if cost requires. Backfill performance assumptions in spreadsheet.

I'll attach the short ops notes and the cost spreadsheet. We should confirm SRE bandwidth and whether Acme wants cloud marketplace billing (makes procurement easier).

Naomi Feldman
Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
